stem: Write reaction to convert methyl bromide into ethyl amine ? Also, comment on the number of carbon atoms in the starting compound and the product.
solution:
Methyl bromide can be converted into ethyl amine in two stage reaction sequence as shown below.

\(\mathrm{CH_3-Br} + \mathrm{KCN} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH_3-CN} + \mathrm{KBr}\)

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CN} \xrightarrow[\text{(reduction)}]{\mathrm{Na/C_2H_5OH}} \mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-NH_2}\)

The starting compound methyl bromide contains one carbon atom while the product ethylamine contains two carbon atoms. A reaction in which number of carbons increases involves a step up reaction. The overall conversion of methyl bromide into ethyl amine is a step up conversion.

stem: Write the scheme for preparation of p-bromoaniline from aniline. Justify your answer.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book numbers this worked example "Problem 13.1" on printed page 295, but it has ALREADY used that same number for the methyl-bromide-to-ethylamine example on printed page 285 — the chapter has two worked examples and both are labelled 13.1. It is referenced here as 13.1b so the two stay distinct. The printed solution below also carries two spelling misprints, preserved as printed: "resonace" for resonance, and "2,4,6-tribromoniline" for 2,4,6-tribromoaniline. Neither affects the chemistry or the answer.]

\(\mathrm{NH_2}\)- group in aniline is highly ring activating and o-/p- directing due to involvement of the lone pair of electrons on 'N' in resonace with the ring. As a result, on reaction with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) it gives 2,4,6-tribromoniline. To get a monobromo product, it is necessary to decrease the ring activating effect of \(\mathrm{-NH_2}\) group. This is done by acetylation of aniline. The lone pair of 'N' in acetanilide is also involved in resonance in the acetyl group. To that extent ring activation decreases.

Hence, acetanilide on bromination gives a monobromo product p-bromoacetanilide. After monobromination the original \(\mathrm{-NH_2}\) group is regenerated. The protection of \(\mathrm{-NH_2}\) group in the form of acetyl group is removed by acid catalyzed hydrolysis to get p-bromoaniline, as shown in the following scheme.

Aniline \(\xrightarrow[\text{base}]{\mathrm{CH_3-CO-Cl}}\) acetanilide \(\xrightarrow[\text{(Acetic acid solvent)}]{\mathrm{Br_2}}\) p-bromoacetanilide \(\xrightarrow[\mathrm{H^{\oplus}}]{\text{hydrolysis}}\) p-bromoaniline
